canonicalisation: UTF-8; frozen membership-authority order; exactly one complete normative QUA identity per ODT text element; whitespace-normalised same-element statement; rule_id + TAB + normative_statement + LF

entries.normative_statement: A formal qualification decision SHALL be supported by attributable evidence.
Evidence SHALL demonstrate the claim being made rather than an easier adjacent claim.
Qualification SHALL distinguish implementation existence from demonstrated satisfaction.
Missing mandatory evidence SHALL remain missing rather than be inferred from unrelated success.
Qualification SHALL NOT silently weaken or reinterpret a governing requirement to make an implementation pass.
A verification procedure SHALL reference the authoritative rule or claim it evaluates.

Where another specification owns an acceptance criterion, registry, matrix or authoritative value, this specification SHALL consume that authority rather than create an independent competing authority.
Duplicate QRR rule identities SHALL fail validation.
Unknown authoritative references SHALL fail validation.
Active mandatory qualification rules SHALL identify at least one credible verification mechanism.
Every normative QUA-* identity present in this specification SHALL occur exactly once in the authoritative QRR.
Verification class SHALL match the nature of the claim.
No verification class SHALL be treated as universally sufficient.
Multiple classes SHALL be used where one class cannot demonstrate the complete claim.
A requirement SHALL NOT be qualified solely through an inappropriate verification class.
Specialised verification-method vocabularies SHALL map deterministically into the canonical qualification-class model.
No single result SHALL be treated as proof of all qualification dimensions.
Each formal release claim SHALL identify the dimensions relevant to it.
Mandatory pass criteria SHALL be defined before a formal result is interpreted as PASS.
Verification SHALL identify the claim under test before execution.
Expected rejection tests SHALL define both expected rejection class and acceptable failure scope.
Verification procedures SHALL identify environmental assumptions capable of affecting the result.
Where qualification depends upon a selectable implementation path, the verification plan SHALL identify the path or paths exercised.
A qualification item SHALL identify mandatory prerequisite decisions, capability classifications and controlled artifacts required before execution.
Qualification SHALL NOT silently invent a capability classification merely because a test happens to succeed or fail.
IMPLEMENTED SHALL NOT imply PASS.
QUALIFIED SHALL require applicable qualification evidence.
NOT_APPLICABLE SHALL require justification for an otherwise mandatory item.
Implementation state SHALL NOT be substituted for formal result state.
PASS SHALL NOT be recorded when mandatory evidence is absent.
Harness failure SHALL NOT be reported as UNSUPPORTED merely to avoid FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE.
NOT_RUN SHALL remain distinct from UNSUPPORTED.
INCONCLUSIVE SHALL NOT become PASS through aggregation.
EXPECTED_REJECTION SHALL require the expected class of rejection.
EXPECTED_REJECTION SHALL require acceptable failure scope.
Unexpected process termination SHALL NOT satisfy EXPECTED_REJECTION.
Waived failures SHALL remain visible as waivers rather than being rewritten as PASS.
Crash-evidence collection MAY preserve diagnostics after such failure but SHALL NOT convert the failure into protocol recovery or PASS.
Unknown binaries SHALL NOT support formal release claims.
Evidence SHALL remain attributable to the binary and configuration actually tested.
Replacing the tested binary SHALL require a new qualification identity unless equivalence is itself formally established.
Instrumented and production binaries SHALL not be silently treated as identical evidence subjects when instrumentation changes relevant behaviour or limits.
Evidence dependent upon a selectable implementation path SHALL identify the path exercised.
Requirement-level results SHALL be traceable from the Qualification Manifest.
Known failures SHALL NOT be silently omitted.
Unsupported capabilities SHALL be represented explicitly.
Formal evidence artifacts SHALL have integrity identities or cryptographic digests where practical.
An evidence manifest SHALL identify artifacts belonging to the qualification run.
Artifact substitution SHALL be detectable where release claims depend upon artifact identity.
Historical qualification results SHOULD be retained immutably, append-only or otherwise tamper-evidently where practical.
Re-running qualification SHALL create a new result identity rather than silently rewriting historical evidence.
Evidence retention SHALL obey secret-handling requirements.
Missing evidence SHALL remain visibly missing rather than be silently reconstructed from unrelated later runs.
Production qualification SHALL contain evidence that core-dump handling for secret-bearing processes has been explicitly considered under the governing security/operations policy.
Orphan mandatory requirements SHALL be detectable.
Duplicate or unknown requirement/rule identities SHALL be detectable.
Dangling implementation, test, evidence or claim references SHALL be detectable.
A mandatory item marked QUALIFIED SHALL have applicable evidence.
A release claim SHALL reference at least one governing requirement.
Formal tests SHALL identify applicable requirements/rules they verify.
Registry-validation failure SHALL prevent formal release qualification.
Unresolved mandatory qualification prerequisites SHALL be detectable.
Evidence from a superseded implementation SHALL NOT automatically qualify its replacement.
Evidence MAY be reused only when qualification-impact analysis establishes continuing applicability.
A stronger-looking but irrelevant test SHALL NOT substitute for the verification class required by the claim.
Inspection evidence SHALL identify exactly what was inspected.
Inspection SHALL NOT claim dynamic behaviour it cannot demonstrate.
Analysis SHALL state assumptions and authoritative inputs.
Analytical arithmetic SHALL use governing limit/expression semantics rather than informal approximations where exactness is required.
Differential agreement SHALL NOT by itself prove that either implementation is correct where both may share the same defect.
Differential disagreement SHALL be investigated rather than resolved by automatically preferring the faster, newer or reference-labelled implementation.

Qualification of the Assembly foundation SHALL include applicable ABI, syscall, arithmetic, memory, pool/resource, external-ABI and stack-boundary verification required by the Assembly Engineering Standard.
Final-machine-code qualification SHALL inspect the production-linked artifact where the governing Assembly rule requires instruction-baseline or disassembly evidence.
CPU instruction-baseline qualification SHALL verify that instructions unavailable to the baseline CPU profile do not appear on unguarded execution paths.
Critical linked routines identified by the Assembly Engineering Standard SHALL receive applicable final disassembly/binary inspection.
Boundary tests SHALL test both accepted and rejected sides of important limits where meaningful.
Tests SHALL NOT assume that one successful nominal case establishes boundary correctness.
Fragmentation boundaries SHOULD be selected independently of parser-preferred boundaries.
Expected failure SHALL verify failure reason/scope where that distinction is part of the requirement.
Externally reachable discrete configured maxima SHALL receive below-limit, at-limit and above-limit qualification where meaningful; N−1/N/N+1 is the canonical procedure for discrete maxima.
Applicable finite deadlines SHALL receive just-before/at/just-after qualification unless an equivalent stronger deterministic procedure is documented.
Negative testing SHALL verify containment, not merely rejection.
Invalid remote input SHALL not qualify as correctly rejected merely because the process crashed.
Rejection at an unnecessarily destructive scope SHALL fail where a smaller scope is required.
Conformance SHALL be evaluated against the declared Standards Register baseline.
Test-suite behaviour SHALL NOT override the governing standard merely because the suite expects it.
A standards ambiguity or suspected suite defect SHALL be recorded rather than silently resolved through implementation mimicry.
Unsupported optional capabilities SHALL remain distinguishable from failed required conformance.
Interoperability success with one implementation SHALL NOT establish universal conformance.
Peer disagreement SHALL be investigated against the applicable standard.
Independent peers SHOULD come from genuinely independent implementation lineages where practicable.
Known peer-specific exceptions SHALL remain visible in evidence.
Browser success SHALL supplement rather than replace protocol conformance.
Browser qualification SHALL verify the actual protocol negotiated rather than assume it.
A browser fallback to another supported protocol SHALL not be reported as successful qualification of the originally intended protocol.
Fuzz harnesses SHALL preserve semantic preconditions of the target sufficiently to exercise meaningful code.
Fuzz findings SHALL be reduced to deterministic regression cases where practicable.
Absence of a fuzz-discovered crash SHALL NOT be represented as proof of total correctness.
Known unresolved fuzz failures SHALL remain visible in formal qualification evidence.
A non-crashing fuzz input SHALL be considered a valid finding when it violates applicable progress, resource, work, output, reclamation, failure-scope or invariant requirements.
Resource-aware fuzz oracles SHALL reference applicable INV-*, LIM-*, resource-accounting or qualification rules where available.
Fault injection SHALL identify the injected fault and injection point.
Qualification SHALL verify expected containment and reclamation after the injected fault.
A fault-injection mechanism SHALL NOT silently alter unrelated acceptance criteria.
Qualification-only fault machinery SHALL not be present or active in production unless explicitly designed and approved.
Simulated network impairment SHALL identify its impairment model and SHALL not be conflated with arbitrary internal code-fault injection.
Resource qualification SHALL identify the applicable ELM.
Qualification SHALL distinguish configured capacity from observed occupancy.
Failure to reach a configured maximum during a test SHALL NOT by itself prove the maximum safe.
Capacity analysis and runtime boundary testing SHOULD be combined where practical.
Externally retained kernel/provider state SHALL not be silently excluded from claims that purport to describe total retained resources.
RSS SHALL NOT be treated as equivalent to direct configured userspace capacity.
Provider hidden allocation SHALL be identified as a limitation where it prevents a stronger total-memory claim.
Instrumentation-induced memory changes SHALL be identified.
Production memory claims SHALL not silently rely on qualification-build object sizes where they differ.
Historical work SHALL remain represented where governing rules require it after transient objects are reclaimed.
A memory bound SHALL NOT be treated as proof of a work bound.
Qualification SHALL exercise inputs designed to maximise work relative to useful progress.
Output qualification SHALL distinguish application payload from protocol-generated amplification where required.
Adversarial resource scenarios required by governing Architecture, Requirements or Security rules SHALL have stable scenario identity and attributable evidence.
RAF evidence SHALL define numerator and denominator explicitly.
RAF dimensions SHALL NOT be silently combined into one unitless score where their units differ.
Qualification SHALL include hostile/adversarial workloads capable of approaching the relevant amplification boundary.
A RAF claim SHALL identify whether it is analytically bounded, empirically measured, or both.
RAF evidence SHALL identify the adversarial scenario or input model used where the result depends upon hostile workload shape.
Qualification SHALL distinguish network admission from expensive cryptographic admission.
Crypto-admission evidence SHALL identify work, state and rejection behaviour.
Per-connection protection alone SHALL not qualify distributed-load protection.
Failed handshakes SHALL be included in historical work/accounting evidence where governing rules require it.
Expected persistent state SHALL be distinguished from leaked state.
Grace-transient state SHALL be observed through the applicable grace period.
External-completion-pending state SHALL not become an unlimited exemption.
Unexplained retained state SHALL prevent qualification PASS.
Confirmed leak SHALL fail applicable qualification.
Reclamation qualification SHALL verify resource-accounting convergence as well as object disappearance where applicable.
Configured exhaustion SHALL produce deterministic behaviour.
Ordinary exhaustion SHALL not be accepted as correct if it manifests as corruption or undefined behaviour.
Pressure transitions SHALL be tested at applicable boundaries.
Recovery from pressure SHALL be qualified where recovery is part of the governing state model.
Protected reserve capacity SHALL be tested where required for bounded failure handling.
Endurance PASS SHALL require completion of the declared duration/workload.
A process remaining alive SHALL NOT alone constitute endurance PASS.
Endurance SHALL include post-workload reclamation/quiescence where applicable.
Unexplained monotonic retained-state growth SHALL prevent PASS.
Mandatory endurance evidence SHALL not be omitted merely because the process completed the workload.
A replay artifact SHALL identify build/configuration assumptions required to interpret it.
Fixed regression cases derived from discovered failures SHALL preserve essential failure-triggering semantics.
Replay success after a fix SHOULD become regression evidence rather than replace the original historical failure evidence.
Evidence SHALL identify whether virtual time was active.
Evidence SHALL identify whether deterministic qualification entropy was active.
Production builds SHALL NOT silently activate qualification-only deterministic entropy.
Production builds SHALL NOT silently replace production monotonic time with qualification virtual time.
A deterministic mechanism SHALL NOT be used for qualification where its use invalidates the property being tested, such as production entropy quality.
A formal deterministic protocol replay case SHALL identify its network input sequence.
A replay case using injected faults SHALL identify the injected-fault sequence.
Equivalent controlled replay inputs SHALL reproduce deterministic protocol-state behaviour wherever the tested subsystem is defined to be deterministic.
Production traffic SHALL NOT be recorded by default solely to support deterministic replay.
A security control SHALL NOT be marked qualified solely because its implementation exists.
Threat mitigation status and qualification result SHALL remain distinct.
Qualification SHALL identify residual limitations preventing stronger security claims.
Qualification SHALL inspect the final linked implementation and verify that required clearing behaviour survives assembly and linking.
Source-level zeroisation intent alone SHALL NOT establish final-binary zeroisation qualification.
Qualification SHALL verify that relevant control paths reach required secret-destruction behaviour.
Final-binary inspection SHALL identify the exact binary/disassembly evidence used to support a secret-zeroisation claim.
Qualification builds SHALL be uniquely identifiable.
Instrumentation state SHALL appear in formal evidence.
Qualification instrumentation SHALL not silently change effective limits without corresponding ELM/evidence treatment.
Evidence obtained only under instrumentation SHALL identify any limitation on applicability to production builds.
Assertions SHALL supplement rather than replace hostile-input validation.
Qualification-only time, entropy, fault-injection or replay mechanisms SHALL be mechanically distinguishable from production behaviour.
Formal release qualification SHALL identify the production binary.
Qualification evidence obtained from a distinct instrumented binary SHALL identify the relationship to the production binary.
Production-critical behaviour SHALL receive direct production-binary verification where instrumentation could materially alter the behaviour being claimed.
Binary equivalence claims SHALL be supported rather than assumed.
Every selectable implementation path that materially affects a qualified property SHALL independently satisfy applicable correctness and safety requirements.
Runtime dispatch qualification SHALL verify that supported hardware/configuration selects only valid qualified paths.
Fallback paths SHALL be qualified rather than assumed correct because an accelerated path passes.
Differential testing SHOULD compare reference/straightforward and optimised implementations where practical.
A performance advantage SHALL NOT excuse a semantic discrepancy between supposedly equivalent variants.
Final-machine-code inspection SHALL verify that optional CPU instructions are confined to execution paths whose dispatch guards establish the required CPU capability.
Waived failures SHALL remain visible.
Expired waivers SHALL not satisfy qualification.
A waiver SHALL NOT silently weaken the governing requirement/rule.
Mandatory release blockers SHALL not be waived unless the governing release policy explicitly permits such a waiver.
Waiver presence SHALL appear in the Qualification Manifest and release evidence.
A mandatory FAIL SHALL remain a failure unless an explicitly permitted valid waiver governs release treatment.
Mandatory NOT_RUN SHALL not aggregate to PASS.
Mandatory INCONCLUSIVE SHALL not aggregate to PASS.
EXPECTED_REJECTION SHALL count only toward the negative/adversarial claim it was designed to demonstrate.
Unsupported optional capability SHALL not fail a release when the governing capability authority explicitly declares it unsupported and no governing requirement requires it.
Unsupported required capability SHALL prevent qualification of the corresponding release claim.
A milestone SHALL NOT close formally until every requirement whose first mandatory qualification point is that milestone has a valid qualification disposition.
Later milestone qualification SHALL inherit applicable regression obligations from previously qualified capability.
A milestone SHALL NOT formally close while an applicable mandatory requirement remains unexplained FAILED or BLOCKED.
A deferred or not-yet-applicable requirement SHALL identify why it does not block the current milestone and when qualification becomes mandatory.
Milestone qualification SHALL preserve visible waivers and known failures.
Milestone closure evidence SHALL be attributable to the implementation state that actually reached the milestone.
A milestone SHALL NOT qualify a capability while a governing prerequisite classification required before that milestone remains unresolved.
Marketing or release language SHALL NOT state a stronger technical claim than the evidence supports.
A claim such as “supports HTTP/3” SHALL require applicable conformance/interoperability evidence rather than merely successful parsing of an H3 request.
Compatibility claims SHALL identify material limitations.
Release claims SHALL remain attributable to the exact release artifact.
Substantive technical release claims SHALL have stable RCR identity.
A claim marked qualified SHALL reference applicable requirements and qualification evidence.
Public compatibility claims SHALL NOT exceed the status demonstrated by the governing Compatibility Matrix and qualification evidence.
Performance claims SHALL reference applicable benchmark evidence.
Security claims SHALL reference applicable security requirements/rules and qualification evidence.
Adding capability SHALL inherit applicable regression obligations from previously qualified capability.
Previously qualified behaviour SHALL remain in regression scope unless controlled impact analysis establishes that it is superseded, removed or unaffected.
Release qualification SHALL consume applicable build/provenance evidence required by the Build, Toolchain & Reproducibility Specification.

Where a release provenance claim is made, qualification evidence SHALL identify or reference source revision, build-environment identity, dependency origin/version and binary identity to the extent required by the governing build specification.
Bundle omission SHALL not erase an underlying failure or unsupported capability.
Evidence-bundle generation SHOULD be automated and deterministic where practical.
Bundle contents SHALL remain attributable to the same qualification identity or explicitly identify cross-run evidence dependencies.
Secret-bearing diagnostic artifacts SHALL not be included in broadly distributed evidence bundles without explicit controlled handling.
Qualification SHALL NOT invent benchmark methodology independently of the Performance & Benchmark Specification.
Performance evidence SHALL not substitute for correctness, conformance or robustness evidence.
A performance claim SHALL identify benchmark evidence supporting it.
M0 SHALL NOT be required to implement later HTTP qualification procedures before corresponding functionality exists.
M0 exit SHALL identify every M0-owned requirement and its qualification status.
M0 SHALL establish automated detection of duplicate or unknown requirement identifiers.
M0 SHALL establish a reproducible mechanism for identifying the binary under qualification.
M0 qualification machinery SHALL avoid structures that prevent later rule/evidence registries from joining the common traceability model.
M0 SHALL establish the representation needed to carry inherited regression obligations into later milestones.
M0 closure SHALL distinguish evidence that qualifies qualification infrastructure from evidence that qualifies the M0 implementation foundation itself.
M0 SHALL NOT close solely because qualification machinery exists; applicable M0 foundation requirements SHALL also have valid qualification dispositions.
Prior PASS evidence SHALL not automatically survive a material implementation change.
Strengthening a test does not retroactively strengthen historical evidence.
Changing a governing limit SHALL trigger impact analysis for evidence depending upon that limit.
Changing a supported capability SHALL trigger impact analysis for relevant conformance, interoperability, browser and release claims.
Changing a shared implementation component SHALL trigger regression-impact analysis for all qualified capabilities depending upon it.
Removing a test from the active regression set SHALL require an explicit traceable reason.
A previously qualified capability SHALL NOT silently lose regression coverage because a later capability becomes the current development focus.
A change to a qualification prerequisite or capability classification SHALL trigger impact analysis for qualification evidence dependent upon that prerequisite.
